اللهم بسطوة جبروت قهرك وبسرعة إغاثة نصرك وبغيرتك لانتهاك حرماتك وبحمايتك لمن احتمى بآياتك أسألك يا الله يا سميع يا قريب يا مجيب يا سريع يا منتقم يا شديد البطش يا جبار يا قهار يا من لا يعجزه قهر الجبابرة ولا يعظم عليه هلاك المتمردة من الملوك والأكاسرة أن تجعل كيد من كاد لي في نحره ومكر من مكر بي عائدا عليه وحفرة من حفر لي واقعا فيها ومن نصب لي شبكة الخداع اجعله يا سيدي مساقا إليها ومصادا فيها وأسيرا لديها اللهم بحق كهيعص اكفنا العدا ولقهم الردى واجعلهم لكل حبيب فدا وسلط عليهم عاجل النقمة في اليوم والغد. اللهم بدد شملهم، اللهم فرق جمعهم، اللهم أقلل عددهم، اللهم اجعل الدائرة عليهم، اللهم أرسل العذاب إليهم، اللهم أخرجهم عن دائرة الحلم واسلبهم مدد الإمهال وغل أيديهم واربط على قلوبهم ولا تبلغهم الآمال. اللهم مزقهم كل ممزق مزقته لأعدائك انتصارا لأنبيائك ورسلك وأوليائك اللهم انتصر لنا لأحبائك على أعدائك، اللهم لا تمكن الأعداء فينا ولا تسلطهم علينا بذنوبنا حم حم حم حم حم حم حم الأمر وجاء النصر فعلينا لا ينصرون حم عسق حمايتنا مما نخاف، اللهم قنا شر الأسواء ولا تجعلنا محلا للبلوى، اللهم أعطنا أمل الرجاء يا من بفضله لفضله نسأل - نسألك العجل العجل إلهي الإجابة الإجابة يا من أجاب نوحا في قومه يا من نصر إبراهيم على أعدائه يا من رد يوسف على يعقوب يا من كشف ضر أيوب يا من أجاب دعوة زكريا يا من قبل تسبيح يونس بن متى نسألك بأسرار أصحاب هذه الدعوات أن تقبل ما به دعوناك وأن تعطينا ما سألناك أعجزنا وعدك الذي وعدته لعبادك المؤمنين لا إله إلا أنت سبحانك إني كنت من الظالمين انقطعت آمالنا وعزتك إلا منك وخاب رجاؤنا وحقك إلا فيك. إن أبطأت غارة الأرحام وابتعدت فأقرب الشيء منا غارة الله يا غارة الله جدي السير مسرعة في حل عقدتنا يا غارة الله عدت العادون وجاروا ورجونا الله مجيرا وكفى بالله وليا وكفى بالله نصيرا حسبنا الله ونعم الوكيل حسبنا الله ونعم الوكيل حسبنا الله ونعم الوكيل لا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله العلي العظيم استجب لنا آمين لا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله العلي العظيم استجب لنا آمين لا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله العلي العظيم استجب لنا آمين فقطع دابر القوم الذين ظلموا والحمد لله رب العالمين وصلى الله على سيدنا محمد النبي الأمي وعلى آله وصحبه وسلم

Notes to Authors

It the policy of this Journal to publish articles in English in all fields of ISLAM provided they are of a high caliber and contribute to the fundamental knowledge of the religion. In keeping with the universal nature of Islam, this journal is not intended to reflect any political, regional, or nationalistic bias. Articles containing unwarranted attacks, direct or implied, against any other religion, sect, belief, or ideology, shall not be accepted for publication. The journal's sole objective is to work within the framework of ISLAM towards a full appreciation of God's message to all humanity.

The journal recognizes the sources of Islamic knowledge to be the Qur'an, the Sunna, analogy (Qiyās), consensus (Ijmā'), and personal thought (Ijtihād). However, THE QUR'AN shall be the ultimate reference. Only statements in full agreement with the Qur'an shall represent the journal's official stand. All other statements, or statements subject to various interpretations shall represent only the author's personal viewpoint.

Manuscripts submitted for publication should be typed, double spaced. Only one copy is required. All Qur'anic quotations must be accompanied by the number(s) of sura(s), and the number(s) of verse(s). Colons should separate the number of sura from the number(s) of verse(s) (e.g. 17:28-33). A group of verses from the same sura should be separated from each other by commas (e.g. 17:28-33, 51, 60-62). When more than one sura are involved, a semi-colon should separate the different suras (e.g. 17:28-33, 51, 60-62; 23:16; 36:9-11, 19-25, 44). The journal will undertake to add the Arabic text to all Qur'anic translations. This is to avoid the inadvertent mental re-translation to an Arabic composition which is different from the original.

Every Hadīth should be accompanied by its sources (transmitters) and the reference book where it may be found. If the transmitter(s) and/or the reference book were not known, this should be stated clearly.

by Professor M. Farid Wajdi

ISLAM: Its Mission in the World

2. CONDEMNATION OF THE PRINCIPLE OF BLIND IMITATION

Of all his achievements as writer, editor of Nour-el-Islam, and Professor at Al-Azhar University, Dr. Wajdi is better known for his famous Qur'anic commentary. This series of articles, which were written by him in Arabic, promises to be a most cherished feature by ALL readers of Islam.

In all ages throughout the human history, reformers were never confronted with a stronger obstacle than that of blind imitation of forefathers and leaders of old religions. This inaction has been the cause of the persistence to this day of corrupted religions whose survival in our times is a slur on the human intellect. It was equally responsible for the continual existence of certain sects which exploited the ignorance of people who were otherwise well-fitted to take their place among the rising nations but have for this reason remained in stygian darkness down to the present day.

Only one who has made a thorough study of the religions professed by the majority of contemporary nations as well as of the few hundred minor divisions derived therefrom, could appreciate the pernicious influence exercised by blind imitation over the life of people and the harm involved in the consequent antagonism to learning and reason. Next to the establishment of its principal beliefs, Islam has striven against the tendency of blind imitation into which people have long lapsed without having it examined or assayed by reason.

Indeed, this rational idea could never have been conceived by minds in those dark and remote times when humanity was yet under age. But when humanity attained maturity in the generations that followed, this idea became an essential element of the universal religion which was ordained by the Lord in His last dispensation, not only to conform with the momentous intellectual development that took place, but also to rouse the religious sentiment in the hearts of men and inspire them to still greater and higher attainments.

Those interested in the investigation of human affairs of recent times will find out that souls have discarded all moral restraints and have fallen an easy prey to unbridled passion and wickedness while the religious sentiment

which constitutes the supreme moral power mitigating those excesses, has become incapable to discharge its function in many a nation. It was on account of this that other agents were sought to counteract those excesses. Some have sought such agents in science, in the power of public opinion or in some human instinct. But the investigator who goes deeply into the initial causes of things, will soon realize that, of all human instincts, the religious sentiment is best suited to counteract those excesses and to wield the most beneficial influence over the souls of men. If, however, it has become unequal to the task in certain nations, it is only on account of the weakness which affected their religions and which was the outcome of what was impressed on the people as being traditional matters to be followed or disregarded as a whole. But if they knew that a religion existed which severely censures imitation and imitators, and insists on reasoning and consideration, a religion whose beliefs are founded on evidence and truth, and is withal framed in a system which surpasses that of modern scientific investigation in reasoning and accuracy, their hopes in regaining the influence of religion will be roused again. For once this influence is regained the religious sentiment is awakened and its power will once more be felt in the guidance of men and in setting up a virtuous civilization for the world.

It was for this reason that Islam has striven hard to overcome the obstacle of blind imitation and has attempted to do this by different ways of reasoning aiming thereby at three objects:

1. To spread its life-giving principles calculated to revive humanity in its later days.
2. To conserve for the religious sentiment its intrinsic power which enables it to restrain the human passions and safeguard the people from being carried away by wickedness.
3. To render the system of religious investigation more advanced and more accurate than that of scientific investigation so that the latter may not overwhelm the former and put it into insignificance.

This is a great objective at which Islam aimed so that reason may not hold undisputed sway over souls independent of the religious sentiment which the Lord has set to mitigate the brutal tendencies attendant on the human state and which no intellectual culture could restrain.

This could only come about by convincing reason, by proof, to give due regard to that sentiment and to admit the power exercised by it. Thus, reason will not concede unless that sentiment is established on a like system of research and investigation and is equally free of any traces of imitation unsupported by material or mental evidence.

By so doing, Islam has succeeded to associate reason with the religious sentiment for the first time in the history of religions. It has succeeded, on the strength of these two great principles, to raise a nation which attained to the height of human progress and took the lead in both moral and scientific culture as well as in the religious leadership of the world. Islam was thus rendered equal to establish the highest civilization on earth without the least conflict between religion and reason and without people degenerating in their morals and propensities as is the case in the present day civilization.

Let us now consider how far has Islam succeeded to fulfill this great project.

Islam was revealed at a time when people were the slaves of false and corrupted religions which they inherited from their forefathers and from which they could not be moved. Any one who wished to move them therefrom was regarded by them as a bitter enemy merely because he attempted to bring about a reform.

The campaign was first opened by admonitions and threats thus awakening in men the instinct of reasoning and urging them to reflection and consideration of the sad end to which past nations have come. This done, Islam began to attack the main cause which prevented them to consider any reform viz. the blind imitation of their forefathers even though they were completely in the wrong. In this connection the Lord says:

وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمُ اتَّبِعُوا مَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ قَالُوا بَلْ نَتَّبِعُ مَا أَلْفَيْنَا عَلَيْهِ آبَاءَنَا أَوْلَوْ كَانَ آبَاؤُهُمْ لَا يَعْقِلُونَ شَيْئًا وَلَا يَهْتَدُونَ وَمَثَلُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا كَمَثَلِ الَّذِي يَنْعِقُ بِمَا لَا يَسْمَعُ إِلَّا دُعَاءً وَنِدَاءً صُمٌّ بُكْمٌ عُمْيٌ فَهُمْ لَا يَعْقِلُونَ

And when they are told, "You shall follow what God has sent down," they say, "We follow only what we found our forefathers doing." What if their forefathers lacked both knowledge and guidance?

The allegory of those who disbelieve is like those who parrot whatever they hear without any understanding. They are deaf, dumb, and blind. Thus, they fail to understand. (2:170-171)

In the preceding verses, the Lord has given a representation of the state of those who were blinded by imitation. He who calls them to righteousness is likened to one who parrots whatever he hears without any comprehension. They are deaf, dumb, blind and devoid of understanding on account of their holding fast to the practices of their forefathers and refusing to put them to the test of reason.

The Lord says that if those unbelievers were asked to follow what the Lord has sent down, they will say "We follow only what we found our forefathers doing," to which the Lord replies rousing the instinct of reason in them: "What if their forefathers lacked both the knowledge and the guidance?"

Then the Lord gave the above representation of them which no one with a whit of pride would tolerate, provoking them thereby to seek an outlet to their sorry state.

In order to move them from this inaction, the Lord then applies different reasoning.

And when they are told, "Come to what God has sent down; come to this Messenger," they say, "Enough for us is what we found our forefathers doing." What if their forefathers had neither knowledge, nor guidance? (5:104)

That is, if the unbelievers were called to follow the guidance of the Qur'an they say the knowledge which we inherited from our forefathers is sufficient for us to which the Lord says:

"Will you still say so if your forefathers lacked both the knowledge and the guidance?"

And in this connection the Lord demanded of the unbelievers to support their claim of the so-called knowledge of their forefathers:

Have you any certain knowledge to substantiate your claim that you may produce to us? (6:148)

In another verse the Lord days:

Bring me a scripture before the Qur'an or some vestiges of ancient knowledge to support your claim if you are truthful. (46:4)

In describing the end of those who imitate their forefathers without any knowledge or a book to guide them, the Lord says:

That is when the leaders shall disown their followers. They shall undergo the punishment and no help shall come to them. The followers shall then say, "If we only get a second chance, we shall disown them as they have disowned us." Thus, God will show them the consequences of their deeds; nothing but sorrow for them, and they shall never exit from the hellfire. (2:166,167)

And:

The Lord will say unto the unbelievers on the Judgment day: "Enter ye into Hell together with nations of jinn and of men who have preceded you;" so oft as one nation enters, it shall curse its sister, until they have all entered in succession, the last of them shall say unto the first: "O Lord, these have led us astray, deal Thou unto them a double punishment of hell-fire;" and the Lord will say: "It shall be doubled unto all, but ye know not."

And the first of them shall say unto the last: "Ye have no advantage over us and we have both been in error; taste ye therefore the punishment for that which ye have done." (7:38-39)

In the preceding verses, the Lord points out that the followers of disbelief are just as culpable as the leaders, for the Lord has endowed all men with reason and required them to distinguish between truth and falsehood. They are therefore equally responsible for their deeds and none of them has an advantage over the other. And when the imitators have asked the Lord to deal a double punishment to their leaders whose example they have imitated, the Lord has adjudged them both responsible and has doubled the punishment to them all. Such was the Lord's warning against persistence in blind imitation.

ISLAM: ITS MISSION IN THE WORLD

Unto the leaders it shall be said:
"This is a company which shall be plunged with you into Hell," to which they shall say: "No welcome is there for them, they shall burn in hell-fire like us." And the followers shall say unto the leaders: "But ye, too! There shall be no welcome for you. It was ye who brought us to this and wretched is the abode." [38:59-60]

On the entry of the unbelievers into Hell, angels shall say to the leaders: "This is a company of your followers that shall be plunged with you into Hell." The leaders shall say: "No welcome is there for them, they have had minds to distinguish between truth and falsehood and their punishment is hell-fire like us." The followers will retort: "No welcome for you either, you have enticed us into this delusion and wretched indeed is our ending."

The Lord (may He be praised and glorified!) has seen fit to impress on us by such variegated forms of eloquence the fact that leaders and followers will come to the one and same evil end, and it avails the latter not to be followers of others so long as they have had minds by which to distinguish between truth and falsehood.

By these solemn admonitions, Islam has demolished the principle of blind imitation of forefathers and has awakened the consciousness of individual responsibility. It has delivered the weak from their bondage to the strong and smashed down the invulnerable walls of exclusiveness which the leaders raised for their own ends.

By demolishing blind imitation Islam has aimed at abolishing a state of ignorance in which men were enslaved to certain sects that made learning and religion an exclusive right only to themselves, and arbitrarily ruled the people even as absolute masters do. They suffered no censure or criticism to be passed on their actions and declined the admission, into their exclusive body, of any outsider though he may have been a noted man of learning and genius.

Should this state of things become established in a nation, learning and religion will be rendered the exclusive right of a sect which will exploit them in their own interest and subject them to the dictates of their passion. In course of time, they will become a collection of stereotyped forms which will check the onward march of progress and stand between nations and the realization of their objectives.

Freedom from the shackles of imitation was the objective of Islam and it has led its people to a perfect state of cooperation between learning and religion as well as between sentiment and reason. Through this cooperation Muslims have attained to the height of progress which gave them the world-leadership for many a century and it is assured that they will regain that leadership once they follow faithfully, the tenets of their glorious religion.

90

by Yūsuf Amīn Walī, Ph.D.
Treasurer, Supreme Council of the Muslim
Young Men's Association, Cairo, Egypt

God's Message to Humanity:
The Ultimate Proof of Authenticity*

God's finalized and completed message to man, namely, the Qur'an, was delivered in the Arabic language.** However, since it is intended for all the people, in all places, at all the times, it carries within its composition the proof of authenticity which can be understood and fully appreciated by anyone regardless of his tongue. On these pages, the reader is presented with physical, examinable, and indisputable evidence that the Qur'an is the unaltered message from the Almighty to His creation. Seekers of the truth shall find herein sure guidance towards their goal. The unfortunate souls who are afflicted with various prejudices shall be utterly blinded (Qur'an 18:57)

The greatest affliction of man is the lack of identity and purpose. Once a correct identity is established, and once the purpose behind our existence is defined, such affliction can, sequentially, be removed. The vast majority of people spend their lives under the pretense that the body constitutes one's identity. Thus, they spend their lives caring for the body, the mere shell of their real self; working, laboring, fighting among themselves, hating, loving, and struggling in the service of their vanishing entity. When it is too late, i.e., when they shed the shell, they discover that their real self was left unfed, undeveloped, and miserably neglected. Their eternal existence in such a feeble state can be rightly described as "hell." On the other hand, those who are fortunate enough to overcome this identity crisis will be able to define their purpose, place the emphasis during their earthly existence on the right goal, and live and act accordingly. They will realize that developing their eternal entity requires putting the body in the service of the soul, and not the other way around.

*Condensed from the book "Miracle of the Qur'an: Significance of the Mysterious Alphabets" by Rashād Khalifa, Islamic Productions International, Inc., St. Louis, Missouri, USA. 1973.
**It had to be delivered in some language. The Qur'an itself states that its language is immaterial; that the believers shall grasp the full message therein, regardless of their mother tongue; and that even the Arabic-speaking people will not understand it unless they qualify therefor by sincerity and devotion (6:25, 18:57; 4:44; 56:77-79.)

ISLAM 1394/1974, 1(2): 91-104

GOD'S MESSAGE TO HUMANITY

Our Creator has informed us of the ways and means of developing and caring for the soul. His message, the one and only message, started with the creation of Adam, the first man; the first messenger. Subsequent messengers, such as Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus, and Muhammad (may God bestow His blessings and peace upon them), delivered the same message whereby man can feed and develop his real self. With the arrival of God's final messenger, THE MESSAGE was finalized, and the Almighty Himself vowed to preserve it for all subsequent generations, and to protect it from alteration or distortion(1). Moreover, the Almighty has vowed to embed in His message such proof of authenticity that each generation can witness; leaving no excuse for anyone to disbelieve(2). This article, which is but a glimpse from a vast computerized study of the Qur'an (3), offers an example of the visible miracles which are embedded in the Qur'an to prove its authenticity. Only those completely enslaved by worldly matters will deny the indisputable proof presented here. To appreciate this evidence which comes to all of humanity from their Creator, one needs no special knowledge of the Qur'an's language.

The Qur'anic Initials

One of the unique features of the Qur'an is the occurrence at the beginning of certain suras of alphabets which bear no apparent meanings. These alphabets, henceforth called "Qur'anic Initials," are not known in any other literary work.

Of the 114 suras in the Qur'an 28 begin with one set of Qur'anic initials, and one sura is prefixed with two sets of Qur'anic initials. Each set of Qur'anic initials consists of a number of letters ranging between one and five. The different sets of Qur'anic initials and the suras where they occur are listed in Table 1. As shown in that table, there are 14 different sets of Qur'anic initials, and the number of letters which participate in the make-up of these initials is also 14. The 14 letters involved in the formation of Qur'anic initials are Alif (A), Ḥā (Ḥ), Rā (R), Sīn (S), Ṣād (Ṣ), Ṭā (Ṭ), ‘Ayn (‘A), Qāf (Q), Kāf (K), Lām (L), Mīm (M), Nūn (N), Hā (H), and Yā (Y). These letters are known in the Muslim literature, more specifically among the Sufi mystics, as "the illumination letters (الحروف النورانية)." The other half of the alphabet, the 14 letters not involved, are known as "the darkness letters (الحروف الظلمانية)."

The suras which contain Qur'anic initials are listed in their recorded sequence in Table 2.

This article will deal with the miraculous features embedded in only two sets of these Qur'anic initials, namely, Qāf (Q) and Ṭā Sīn Mīm (ṬSM). For the complete computerized study of all 14 sets of Qur'anic initials, the reader may consult reference 3 listed below.

The Qur'anic Initial Qāf (Q)

There are two suras in the Qur'an which bear this initial, namely, sura Al-Shūrā (number 42) and sura Qāf (number 50). Although sura Al-Shūrā is more than twice as long as sura Qāf, these two Qāf-initialed suras contain the same number of the letter Qāf (Q), 57. At this point, we must stop and reflect on the significance of this observation. To derive correct conclusions, the following points should be borne in mind:

1. This observation is an undeniable fact; no speculation or guesswork is involved. It is a fact that anyone, anywhere in the world, can establish for himself, regardless of his language. The only prerequisite would be familiarity with one letter of the Arabic alphabet; the letter Qāf (Q). The letter looks like this: ق . When placed at the beginning of a word, it looks like this: قـ . When placed in the middle of the word, the letter Qāf (Q) looks like this: ـقـ . At the end of a word, the letter looks like this: ـق .

With this minute amount of information, any person can look up the Qur'an, count the frequency of the letter Qāf in sura Al-Shūrā (No. 42) and in sura Qāf (No. 50). This person will physically establish THE FACT that the only two suras in the Qur'an which are initialed with letter Qāf contain the same number of this letter, namely 57.

2. The second fact one must bear in mind is that the Qur'an was revealed over a period of 23 years. Its verses came to us widely separated from each other both in time and place. Thus, sura Al-Shūrā, for example, contains 4 verses which were revealed in Medina, namely, verses 23, 24, 25, and 27. The other 49 verses were revealed, separately, in Mecca (300 miles from Medina). Sura Qāf consists of 44 Meccan verses and one Medinian verse (No. 38).

These historical facts are significant, since they point out to us that the Author of the Qur'an knew in advance the alphabetical distribution within the Qur'an. One can readily see from the revelation system that such knowledge is beyond the ability of any human or group of humans(4). The evidence is overwhelmingly presented in this minute glimpse of the total study that the Qur'an could not be man-made. To indicate this advance knowledge to the recipients of His message, the Almighty Author placed the initial Qāf (Q) at the beginning of these two suras which contain the same number of this particular letter.

Racial Concepts
Racism has reference to a socio-political policy or system which is based on the exaggeration of racial differences or on prejudice in favor of a certain race. Race itself is difficult to define. Many writers have spoken customarily of a Greek “race”, a Nordic “race”, an Anglo-Saxon “race”, an Aryan “race” and so on, but racial nomenclature is illusive. Though mankind is comprised of a number of different groups which are physically distinguishable in some degree from one another, “the differences between the four major groups of man and between the ethnic groups comprising them merely represent a distribution of variations which . . . occur more frequently in one group than they do in another . . . Not one of the major groups of man is unmixed, nor is any one of its ethnic groups pure; all are, indeed, much mixed and of exceedingly complex descent. Nor is there any scientific justification for overzealous or emotional claims that any one of them is in any way superior to another.”(1) In general, “race” means the major divisions of mankind which share certain common physical characteristics such as skin color, facial structure and texture of hair. The actual enshrining of discrimination on the pedestal of science, however, awaited later centuries.

In 20th century industrialized societies minorities are often assigned to menial positions reserved for social outcasts or inferiors. The Muslims did not treat Bilāl in this manner. Indeed, he was appointed the treasurer of the Muslim community, a position of utmost responsibility and trust. Bilāl was renowned also as the first mu'adhdhin, which was a position of respected spiritual leadership. He was an active participant - not an orderly or attendant - in all of the battles fought to defend the Muslim community, slaying in the battle of Badr his former owner, Umayyah. There is no analogy at all to the degrading references to blacks even in America in the case of Bilāl. The Muslims never called him a "nigger", a "coon" or a "Sambo". Rather, this former slave was affectionately called "Sayyidunā Bilāl" - our master Bilāl - by the Muslims.

Similarly, in America and most European countries, racial intermarriage has been long legally taboo, just as it still is in white-ruled nations like Rhodesia and South Africa. We have honored (karramnā) the children of Adam... and conferred on them special favors, above a great part of our creation. [17:70]

No race or ethnic group comprising "the children of Adam" has been excluded from this honor or nobility (karāmah) and superiority or preference (faḍl) which God has conferred on mankind over the rest of creation.

As for varieties of color, Islam does not consider any hue of skin as being the result of a curse. All complexions are signs of God's creative power.

Among His signs (or, miracles: āyāt) is the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the differences in your languages and complexions. Truly these are signs for those who reflect. [30:22]

No language or color is considered inferior and the very existence of diversity is indicative of God's miraculous, complex creative ability. The brown or black complexion is equally a miracle or marvel (āyah) as the white or yellow complexion.

O mankind. We created you all from a single pair, and made you various races (shu'ūb) and tribes so that you may be mutually acquainted. [49:13]

Bernard Lewis passes over this phenomenal statement, having blurred its import by translating shu‘ūb (races) as the vague term “confederacies” and asserting that the main point being made by it is “clearly social rather than racial.”(29) This assumption is incorrect. Shu‘ūb does refer to “races”. Dr. A. J. Distinction between people on the basis of race, color or wealth or on any other basis is artificial and should not be tolerated.”(31)

Islam insists that racial variety should be a means of mutual attraction, and this has been the function of racial variety during the many millenia in which the human population interbred extensively. Islam condemns racial discrimination as ignorance and goes beyond the requirement of mere racial tolerance. Islam calls for racial appreciation, mutual respect, a positive human brotherhood based on love for God and man.

A true understanding of Islam requires, as a minimum, a reasonable understanding of its message, the Qur'an. While many people acquire a distorted picture of the religion by observing some aspects of the actions, history, or personal conduct of its professed followers, the readers of this series are presented with an opportunity to grasp the basic principles of true Islam. Readers who are familiar with the various Qur'anic translations will appreciate the fact that this is the first English rendering of the Qur'an's meanings by a Muslim Arab. pages.arabic_text: وَإِذْ قَالَ رَبُّكَ لِلْمَلَٰئِكَةِ إِنِّى جَاعِلٌ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ خَلِيفَةًۖ قَالُوٓا۟ أَتَجْعَلُ فِيهَا مَن يُفْسِدُ فِيهَا وَيَسْفِكُ ٱلدِّمَآءَ وَنَحْنُ نُسَبِّحُ بِحَمْدِكَ وَنُقَدِّسُ لَكَۖ قَالَ إِنِّىٓ أَعْلَمُ مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ (٣٠) وَعَلَّمَ ءَادَمَ ٱلْأَسْمَآءَ كُلَّهَا ثُمَّ عَرَضَهُمْ عَلَى ٱلْمَلَٰئِكَةِ فَقَالَ أَنۢبِـُٔونِى بِأَسْمَآءِ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ إِن كُنتُمْ صَٰدِقِينَ (٣١) قَالُوا۟ سُبْحَٰنَكَ لَا عِلْمَ لَنَآ إِلَّا مَا عَلَّمْتَنَآۖ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلْعَلِيمُ ٱلْحَكِيمُ (٣٢) قَالَ يَٰٓـَٔادَمُ أَنۢبِئْهُم بِأَسْمَآئِهِمْۖ فَلَمَّآ أَنۢبَأَهُم بِأَسْمَآئِهِمْ قَالَ أَلَمْ أَقُل لَّكُمْ إِنِّىٓ أَعْلَمُ غَيْبَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ وَأَعْلَمُ مَا تُبْدُونَ وَمَا كُنتُمْ تَكْتُمُونَ (٣٣) وَإِذْ قُلْنَا لِلْمَلَٰئِكَةِ ٱسْجُدُوا۟ لِءَادَمَ فَسَجَدُوٓا۟ إِلَّآ إِبْلِيسَ أَبَىٰ وَٱسْتَكْبَرَ وَكَانَ مِنَ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ (٣٤) وَقُلْنَا يَٰٓـَٔادَمُ ٱسْكُنْ أَنتَ وَزَوْجُكَ ٱلْجَنَّةَ وَكُلَا مِنْهَا رَغَدًا حَيْثُ شِئْتُمَا وَلَا تَقْرَبَا هَٰذِهِ ٱلشَّجَرَةَ فَتَكُونَا مِنَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ (٣٥) فَأَزَلَّهُمَا ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ عَنْهَا فَأَخْرَجَهُمَا مِمَّا كَانَا فِيهِۖ وَقُلْنَا ٱهْبِطُوا۟ بَعْضُكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّۖ وَلَكُمْ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ مُسْتَقَرٌّ وَمَتَٰعٌ إِلَىٰ حِينٍ (٣٦)

SURA AL-BAQARAH 2:37-50

37 Then Adam received from his Lord certain commands whereby God redeemed him. Surely, He is the Redeemer, the Merciful. 38 I said, “Go down therefrom, all of you, and when My guidance comes to you, those who follow My guidance shall have no fear, nor shall they grieve. 39 As for those who disbelieve and reject My Revelations, they shall deserve the hellfire. They shall abide therein eternally.”

(The Children of Israel)

40 O Children of Israel, be appreciative of the favors which I bestowed upon you; fulfill My covenant, that I may fulfill your covenant; you shall reverence Me; 41 You shall believe in what I reveal herein confirming what you have; do not be the first to reject it; you shall not trade away My revelations for a cheap material gain; you shall observe piety towards Me. 42 Do not confound the truth with falsehood, nor conceal the truth deliberately. 43 You shall observe the Ṣalāt prayers, pay the Zakāt charity (due alms), and bow (in prayer) with those who bow. 44 Do you order people to be righteous, while forgetting your own selves, even though you know the scripture? Have you not any understanding? 45 Seek help in perseverance and in the Ṣalāt. Such is a difficult task, but not so for those who humble themselves; 46 who believe that they shall face their Lord; that they shall return to Him. 47 O Children of Israel, be appreciative of the favors which I bestowed upon you; I set you apart from all beings. 48 Beware of the day when no soul can avail another soul, no intercession can be accepted therefrom, no ransom can be paid, and no one can be helped.

(Deliverance from Egypt)

49 Recall that I saved you from the Pharaoh’s people who inflicted severe persecution upon you; they slaughtered your sons and spared your daughters. Such was an exacting trial from your Lord. 50 Recall that I parted the sea for you; thus, I saved you and drowned the Pharaoh’s people as you watched.

pages.arabic_text: فَتَلَقَّىٰ آدَمُ مِن رَّبِّهِ كَلِمَاتٍ فَتَابَ عَلَيْهِ ۚ إِنَّهُ هُوَ التَّوَّابُ الرَّحِيمُ (37) قُلْنَا اهْبِطُوا مِنْهَا جَمِيعًا ۖ فَإِمَّا يَأْتِيَنَّكُم مِّنِّي هُدًى فَمَن تَبِعَ هُدَايَ فَلَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ (38) وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَكَذَّبُوا بِآيَاتِنَا أُولَٰئِكَ أَصْحَابُ النَّارِ ۖ هُمْ فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ (39) يَا بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ اذْكُرُوا نِعْمَتِيَ الَّتِي أَنْعَمْتُ عَلَيْكُمْ وَأَوْفُوا بِعَهْدِي أُوفِ بِعَهْدِكُمْ وَإِيَّايَ فَارْهَبُونِ (40) وَآمِنُوا بِمَا أَنزَلْتُ مُصَدِّقًا لِّمَا مَعَكُمْ وَلَا تَكُونُوا أَوَّلَ كَافِرٍ بِهِ ۖ وَلَا تَشْتَرُوا بِآيَاتِي ثَمَنًا قَلِيلًا وَإِيَّايَ فَاتَّقُونِ (41) وَلَا تَلْبِسُوا الْحَقَّ بِالْبَاطِلِ وَتَكْتُمُوا الْحَقَّ وَأَنتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ (42) وَأَقِيمُوا الصَّلَاةَ وَآتُوا الزَّكَاةَ وَارْكَعُوا مَعَ الرَّاكِعِينَ (43) أَتَأْمُرُونَ النَّاسَ بِالْبِرِّ وَتَنسَوْنَ أَنفُسَكُمْ وَأَنتُمْ تَتْلُونَ الْكِتَابَ ۚ أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ (44) وَاسْتَعِينُوا بِالصَّبْرِ وَالصَّلَاةِ ۚ وَإِنَّهَا لَكَبِيرَةٌ إِلَّا عَلَى الْخَاشِعِينَ (45) الَّذِينَ يَظُنُّونَ أَنَّهُم مُّلَاقُو رَبِّهِمْ وَأَنَّهُمْ إِلَيْهِ رَاجِعُونَ (46) يَا بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ اذْكُرُوا نِعْمَتِيَ الَّتِي أَنْعَمْتُ عَلَيْكُمْ وَأَنِّي فَضَّلْتُكُمْ عَلَى الْعَالَمِينَ (47) وَاتَّقُوا يَوْمًا لَّا تَجْزِي نَفْسٌ عَن نَّفْسٍ شَيْئًا وَلَا يُقْبَلُ مِنْهَا شَفَاعَةٌ وَلَا يُؤْخَذُ مِنْهَا عَدْلٌ وَلَا هُمْ يُنصَرُونَ (48) وَإِذْ نَجَّيْنَاكُم مِّنْ آلِ فِرْعَوْنَ يَسُومُونَكُمْ سُوءَ الْعَذَابِ يُذَبِّحُونَ أَبْنَاءَكُمْ وَيَسْتَحْيُونَ نِسَاءَكُمْ ۚ وَفِي ذَٰلِكُمْ بَلَاءٌ مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ عَظِيمٌ (49) وَإِذْ فَرَقْنَا بِكُمُ الْبَحْرَ فَأَنجَيْنَاكُمْ وَأَغْرَقْنَا آلَ فِرْعَوْنَ وَأَنتُمْ تَنظُرُونَ (50)

الجزء الأول (٢) سورة البقرة
فَتَلَقَّىٰ ءَادَمُ مِن رَّبِّهِۦ كَلِمَٰتٍ فَتَابَ عَلَيْهِ ۚ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلتَّوَّابُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ (٣٧) قُلْنَا ٱهْبِطُوا۟ مِنْهَا جَمِيعًا ۖ فَإِمَّا يَأْتِيَنَّكُم مِّنِّى هُدًى فَمَن تَبِعَ هُدَاىَ فَلَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ (٣٨) وَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ وَكَذَّبُوا۟ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَآ أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ أَصْحَٰبُ ٱلنَّارِ ۖ هُمْ فِيهَا خَٰلِدُونَ (٣٩) يَٰبَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ ٱذْكُرُوا۟ نِعْمَتِىَ ٱلَّتِىٓ أَنْعَمْتُ عَلَيْكُمْ وَأَوْفُوا۟ بِعَهْدِىٓ أُوفِ بِعَهْدِكُمْ وَإِيَّٰىَ فَٱرْهَبُونِ (٤٠) وَءَامِنُوا۟ بِمَآ أَنزَلْتُ مُصَدِّقًا لِّمَا مَعَكُمْ وَلَا تَكُونُوٓا۟ أَوَّلَ كَافِرٍۭ بِهِۦ ۖ وَلَا تَشْتَرُوا۟ بِـَٔايَٰتِى ثَمَنًا قَلِيلًا وَإِيَّٰىَ فَٱتَّقُونِ (٤١) وَلَا تَلْبِسُوا۟ ٱلْحَقَّ بِٱلْبَٰطِلِ وَتَكْتُمُوا۟ ٱلْحَقَّ وَأَنتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ (٤٢) وَأَقِيمُوا۟ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتُوا۟ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَٱرْكَعُوا۟ مَعَ ٱلرَّٰكِعِينَ (٤٣) أَتَأْمُرُونَ ٱلنَّاسَ بِٱلْبِرِّ وَتَنسَوْنَ أَنفُسَكُمْ وَأَنتُمْ تَتْلُونَ ٱلْكِتَٰبَ ۚ أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ (٤٤) وَٱسْتَعِينُوا۟ بِٱلصَّبْرِ وَٱلصَّلَوٰةِ ۚ وَإِنَّهَا لَكَبِيرَةٌ إِلَّا عَلَى ٱلْخَٰشِعِينَ (٤٥) ٱلَّذِينَ يَظُنُّونَ أَنَّهُم مُّلَٰقُوا۟ رَبِّهِمْ وَأَنَّهُمْ إِلَيْهِ رَٰجِعُونَ (٤٦) يَٰبَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ ٱذْكُرُوا۟ نِعْمَتِىَ ٱلَّتِىٓ أَنْعَمْتُ عَلَيْكُمْ وَأَنِّى فَضَّلْتُكُمْ عَلَى ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ (٤٧) وَٱتَّقُوا۟ يَوْمًا لَّا تَجْزِى نَفْسٌ عَن نَّفْسٍ شَيْـًٔا وَلَا يُقْبَلُ مِنْهَا شَفَٰعَةٌ وَلَا يُؤْخَذُ مِنْهَا عَدْلٌ وَلَا هُمْ يُنصَرُونَ (٤٨) وَإِذْ نَجَّيْنَٰكُم مِّنْ ءَالِ فِرْعَوْنَ يَسُومُونَكُمْ سُوٓءَ ٱلْعَذَابِ يُذَبِّحُونَ أَبْنَآءَكُمْ وَيَسْتَحْيُونَ نِسَآءَكُمْ ۚ وَفِى ذَٰلِكُم بَلَآءٌ مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ عَظِيمٌ (٤٩) وَإِذْ فَرَقْنَا بِكُمُ ٱلْبَحْرَ فَأَنجَيْنَٰكُمْ وَأَغْرَقْنَآ ءَالَ فِرْعَوْنَ وَأَنتُمْ تَنظُرُونَ (٥٠)

51 Recall that when I summoned Moses for forty nights, you worshiped the calf in his absence, and you turned wicked. 52 Yet, I pardoned you thereafter, that you may be appreciative. 53 Recall that I gave Moses the scripture and the statute book, that you may be guided. 54 Recall that Moses told his followers, "You have wronged your souls by worshiping the calf. Therefore, you shall repent to your Creator; you shall kill your ego. This would be best for you with your Creator." Subsequently, God absolved you. Surely, He is the Absolver, most-Merciful. 55 When you said, "O Moses, we shall not believe unless we see God in person," the lightning struck you as you looked. 56 Then, I revived you after you died, that you may be appreciative.

(In Sinai)

57 I shaded you with clouds, and sent down to you manna and quails; "Eat from the good things I provide for you." Indeed, they did no harm to Me, but rather they harmed themselves. 58 When I said, "Go into this village and eat therefrom as you please; enter the gate in humbleness, and speak gently, that I may forgive your sins and reward the virtuous," 59 the evil ones distorted My commandments. Consequently, I showered the evil ones with wrath from the sky due to their wickedness. 60 Recall that when Moses sought water for his followers, I said, "Strike the rock with your staff." Whereupon, twelve springs gushed out therefrom. Thus, each of the tribes had their own water; "Eat and drink from God's provisions, and roam not the earth in corruption."

ظَلَمْتُمْ أَنفُسَكُم بِاتِّخَاذِكُمُ الْعِجْلَ فَتُوبُوا إِلَىٰ بَارِئِكُمْ فَاقْتُلُوا أَنفُسَكُمْ ذَٰلِكُمْ خَيْرٌ لَّكُمْ عِندَ بَارِئِكُمْ فَتَابَ عَلَيْكُمْ ۚ إِنَّهُ هُوَ التَّوَّابُ الرَّحِيمُ
وَإِذْ قُلْتُمْ يَا مُوسَىٰ لَن نُّؤْمِنَ لَكَ حَتَّىٰ نَرَى اللَّهَ جَهْرَةً فَأَخَذَتْكُمُ الصَّاعِقَةُ وَأَنتُمْ تَنظُرُونَ
ثُمَّ بَعَثْنَاكُم مِّن بَعْدِ مَوْتِكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ
وَظَلَّلْنَا عَلَيْكُمُ الْغَمَامَ وَأَنزَلْنَا عَلَيْكُمُ الْمَنَّ وَالسَّلْوَىٰ ۖ كُلُوا مِن طَيِّبَاتِ مَا رَزَقْنَاكُمْ ۖ وَمَا ظَلَمُونَا وَلَٰكِن كَانُوا أَنفُسَهُمْ يَظْلِمُونَ
وَإِذْ قُلْنَا ادْخُلُوا هَٰذِهِ الْقَرْيَةَ فَكُلُوا مِنْهَا حَيْثُ شِئْتُمْ رَغَدًا وَادْخُلُوا الْبَابَ سُجَّدًا وَقُولُوا حِطَّةٌ نَّغْفِرْ لَكُمْ خَطَايَاكُمْ ۚ وَسَنَزِيدُ الْمُحْسِنِينَ
فَبَدَّلَ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا قَوْلًا غَيْرَ الَّذِي قِيلَ لَهُمْ فَأَنزَلْنَا عَلَى الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا رِجْزًا مِّنَ السَّمَاءِ بِمَا كَانُوا يَفْسُقُونَ
وَإِذِ اسْتَسْقَىٰ مُوسَىٰ لِقَوْمِهِ فَقُلْنَا اضْرِب بِّعَصَاكَ الْحَجَرَ ۖ فَانفَجَرَتْ مِنْهُ اثْنَتَا عَشْرَةَ عَيْنًا ۖ قَدْ عَلِمَ كُلُّ أُنَاسٍ مَّشْرَبَهُمْ ۖ كُلُوا وَاشْرَبُوا مِن رِّزْقِ اللَّهِ وَلَا تَعْثَوْا فِي الْأَرْضِ مُفْسِدِينَ

الجزء الأول (٢) سورة البقرة
وَإِذْ وَاعَدْنَا مُوسَىٰ أَرْبَعِينَ لَيْلَةً ثُمَّ اتَّخَذْتُمُ الْعِجْلَ مِن بَعْدِهِ وَأَنتُمْ ظَالِمُونَ ﴿٥١﴾ ثُمَّ عَفَوْنَا عَنكُم مِّن بَعْدِ ذَٰلِكَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ ﴿٥٢﴾ وَإِذْ آتَيْنَا مُوسَى الْكِتَابَ وَالْفُرْقَانَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَهْتَدُونَ ﴿٥٣﴾ وَإِذْ قَالَ مُوسَىٰ لِقَوْمِهِ يَا قَوْمِ إِنَّكُمْ ظَلَمْتُمْ أَنفُسَكُم بِاتِّخَاذِكُمُ الْعِجْلَ فَتُوبُوا إِلَىٰ بَارِئِكُمْ فَاقْتُلُوا أَنفُسَكُمْ ذَٰلِكُمْ خَيْرٌ لَّكُمْ عِندَ بَارِئِكُمْ فَتَابَ عَلَيْكُمْ ۚ إِنَّهُ هُوَ التَّوَّابُ الرَّحِيمُ ﴿٥٤﴾ وَإِذْ قُلْتُمْ يَا مُوسَىٰ لَن نُّؤْمِنَ لَكَ حَتَّىٰ نَرَى اللَّهَ جَهْرَةً فَأَخَذَتْكُمُ الصَّاعِقَةُ وَأَنتُمْ تَنظُرُونَ ﴿٥٥﴾ ثُمَّ بَعَثْنَاكُم مِّن بَعْدِ مَوْتِكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ ﴿٥٦﴾ وَظَلَّلْنَا عَلَيْكُمُ الْغَمَامَ وَأَنزَلْنَا عَلَيْكُمُ الْمَنَّ وَالسَّلْوَىٰ ۖ كُلُوا مِن طَيِّبَاتِ مَا رَزَقْنَاكُمْ ۖ وَمَا ظَلَمُونَا وَلَٰكِن كَانُوا أَنفُسَهُمْ يَظْلِمُونَ ﴿٥٧﴾ وَإِذْ قُلْنَا ادْخُلُوا هَٰذِهِ الْقَرْيَةَ فَكُلُوا مِنْهَا حَيْثُ شِئْتُمْ رَغَدًا وَادْخُلُوا الْبَابَ سُجَّدًا وَقُولُوا حِطَّةٌ نَّغْفِرْ لَكُمْ خَطَايَاكُمْ ۚ وَسَنَزِيدُ الْمُحْسِنِينَ ﴿٥٨﴾ فَبَدَّلَ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا قَوْلًا غَيْرَ الَّذِي قِيلَ لَهُمْ فَأَنزَلْنَا عَلَى الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا رِجْزًا مِّنَ السَّمَاءِ بِمَا كَانُوا يَفْسُقُونَ ﴿٥٩﴾ وَإِذِ اسْتَسْقَىٰ مُوسَىٰ لِقَوْمِهِ فَقُلْنَا اضْرِب بِّعَصَاكَ الْحَجَرَ ۖ فَانفَجَرَتْ مِنْهُ اثْنَتَا عَشْرَةَ عَيْنًا ۖ قَدْ عَلِمَ كُلُّ أُنَاسٍ مَّشْرَبَهُمْ ۖ كُلُوا وَاشْرَبُوا مِن رِّزْقِ اللَّهِ وَلَا تَعْثَوْا فِي الْأَرْضِ مُفْسِدِينَ ﴿٦٠﴾

SURA AL-BAQARAH 2:61-68

61 When you told Moses, “We can no longer tolerate one kind of food; ask your Lord to produce for us earthly crops such as beans, cucumber, garlic, lentils, and onions,” he said, “Do you wish to substitute that which is inferior for that which is good? Go down to the countryside wherein you may find your request.” Thus, humiliation and poverty became their lot, and they incurred wrath from God. That, because they rejected God’s commandments and because they slew the prophets unjustly; because they rebelled and transgressed. 62 Surely, those who believe; those who were Jewish, Christian, or Sabian; any among them who did believe in God and the hereafter, and did good works, shall receive their recompense from their Lord; they shall have no fear, nor shall they grieve.

(The Covenant)

63 Recall that I made a covenant with you, and raised Mount Sinai above you, saying, “You shall uphold this covenant strongly, and remember the contents thereof, that you may achieve piety.” 64 But you turned away thereafter, and were it not for God’s grace towards you and His mercy, you would have been destroyed. 65 You know what happened to those among you who desecrated the Sabbath; I said unto them, “You shall be despicable apes.” 66 Thus, I set them up as an example for their generation, as well as subsequent generations, and an admonition for the pious.

(The Heifer)

67 When Moses said to his followers, “God commands you to sacrifice a heifer,” they said, “Are you kidding us?” He said, “God forbid that I may be so ignorant.” 68 They said, “Ask your Lord to show us what kind of heifer.” Moses said, “He says that she is a heifer which is neither too old, nor too young; of an average age. You shall carry out this command.”

126 ISLAM 1394/1974, 1(2)

الجزء الأول (٢) سورة البقرة
وَإِذْ قُلْتُمْ يَا مُوسَىٰ لَن نَّصْبِرَ عَلَىٰ طَعَامٍ وَاحِدٍ فَادْعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ يُخْرِجْ لَنَا مِمَّا تُنبِتُ الْأَرْضُ مِن بَقْلِهَا وَقِثَّائِهَا وَفُومِهَا وَعَدَسِهَا وَبَصَلِهَا ۖ قَالَ أَتَسْتَبْدِلُونَ الَّذِي هُوَ أَدْنَىٰ بِالَّذِي هُوَ خَيْرٌ ۚ اهْبِطُوا مِصْرًا فَإِنَّ لَكُم مَّا سَأَلْتُمْ ۗ وَضُرِبَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ الذِّلَّةُ وَالْمَسْكَنَةُ وَبَاءُوا بِغَضَبٍ مِّنَ اللَّهِ ۗ ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ كَانُوا يَكْفُرُونَ بِآيَاتِ اللَّهِ وَيَقْتُلُونَ النَّبِيِّينَ بِغَيْرِ الْحَقِّ ۗ ذَٰلِكَ بِمَا عَصَوا وَّكَانُوا يَعْتَدُونَ ٦١ إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَالَّذِينَ هَادُوا وَالنَّصَارَىٰ وَالصَّابِئِينَ مَنْ آمَنَ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ وَعَمِلَ صَالِحًا فَلَهُمْ أَجْرُهُمْ عِندَ رَبِّهِمْ وَلَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ ٦٢ وَإِذْ أَخَذْنَا مِيثَاقَكُمْ وَرَفَعْنَا فَوْقَكُمُ الطُّورَ خُذُوا مَا آتَيْنَاكُم بِقُوَّةٍ وَاذْكُرُوا مَا فِيهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَّقُونَ ٦٣ ثُمَّ تَوَلَّيْتُم مِّن بَعْدِ ذَٰلِكَ ۖ فَلَوْلَا فَضْلُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ وَرَحْمَتُهُ لَكُنتُم مِّنَ الْخَاسِرِينَ ٦٤ وَلَقَدْ عَلِمْتُمُ الَّذِينَ اعْتَدَوْا مِنكُمْ فِي السَّبْتِ فَقُلْنَا لَهُمْ كُونُوا قِرَدَةً خَاسِئِينَ ٦٥ فَجَعَلْنَاهَا نَكَالًا لِّمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيْهَا وَمَا خَلْفَهَا وَمَوْعِظَةً لِّلْمُتَّقِينَ ٦٦ وَإِذْ قَالَ مُوسَىٰ لِقَوْمِهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَأْمُرُكُمْ أَن تَذْبَحُوا بَقَرَةً ۖ قَالُوا أَتَتَّخِذُنَا هُزُوًا ۖ قَالَ أَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ أَنْ أَكُونَ مِنَ الْجَاهِلِينَ ٦٧ قَالُوا ادْعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ يُبَيِّن لَّنَا مَا هِيَ ۚ قَالَ إِنَّهُ يَقُولُ إِنَّهَا بَقَرَةٌ لَّا فَارِضٌ وَلَا بِكْرٌ عَوَانٌ بَيْنَ ذَٰلِكَ ۖ فَافْعَلُوا مَا تُؤْمَرُونَ ٦٨

SURA AL-BAQARAH 2:69-79

69 They said, “Ask your Lord to inform us of her color.” Moses said, “He says that she shall be a yellow heifer; bright-colored and pleasant looking.” 70 They said, “Ask your Lord to point her out for us. The heifers look alike; with God’s help we shall find her.” 71 Moses said, “He says that she is a heifer never humiliated in plowing the land or watering the crops; safe from any blemish.” They said, “Now you have brought the truth;” they sacrificed her, though reluctantly. 72 Then, when you committed a murder and disputed among yourselves, God decided to uncover what you tried to conceal. 73 Thus, I said, “Strike the victim with part of that heifer.” Whereupon, God revived the victim and showed you His signs, that you may understand. 74 Yet, your hearts hardened thereafter and became like rocks or even harder. For there are rocks from which rivers gush out; some rocks crack and gently release water; some rocks even stoop out of reverence for God. God is never unaware of anything you do.

(Distortion of the Scriptures)
75 How do you expect them to believe with you? Some of them used to hear the word of God then deliberately distort it with full understanding thereof. 76 When they meet the believers, they say, “We believe in this,” but when in private with each other, they say, “Inform them not of the scripture revealed to you from God, lest they may use it to support their argument. Do you not understand?” 77 Do they not realize that God knows whatever they hide, as well as whatever they disclose? 78 Among them there are those who have no knowledge of the scripture; they may think that they know it, but in fact they do not. 79 Therefore, woe to those who fabricate the scripture with their own hands, then claim that such writings came from God, seeking thereby a cheap material gain. Woe to them as a consequence of their fabrications; woe to them as a consequence of their deeds.

128 ISLAM 1394/1974, 1(2)

بَقَرَةٌ صَفْرَاءُ
لَوْنُهَا تَسُرُّ النَّاظِرِينَ
إِنَّهُ يَقُولُ
إِنَّهَا بَقَرَةٌ لَّا ذَلُولٌ
تُثِيرُ الْأَرْضَ وَلَا تَسْقِي الْحَرْثَ
مُسَلَّمَةٌ لَّا شِيَةَ فِيهَا
فَذَبَحُوهَا وَمَا كَادُوا يَفْعَلُونَ
فَقُلْنَا اضْرِبُوهُ بِبَعْضِهَا
ثُمَّ قَسَتْ قُلُوبُكُم
مِّن بَعْدِ ذَٰلِكَ فَهِيَ كَالْحِجَارَةِ أَوْ أَشَدُّ قَسْوَةً
وَإِنَّ مِنَ الْحِجَارَةِ
لَمَا يَتَفَجَّرُ مِنْهُ الْأَنْهَارُ
وَإِنَّ مِنْهَا لَمَا يَشَّقَّقُ
فَيَخْرُجُ مِنْهُ الْمَاءُ
وَإِنَّ مِنْهَا لَمَا يَهْبِطُ
مِنْ خَشْيَةِ اللَّهِ
وَمَا اللَّهُ بِغَافِلٍ عَمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ
أَفَتَطْمَعُونَ أَن يُؤْمِنُوا لَكُمْ
وَقَدْ كَانَ فَرِيقٌ مِّنْهُمْ يَسْمَعُونَ كَلَامَ اللَّهِ
ثُمَّ يُحَرِّفُونَهُ مِن بَعْدِ مَا عَقَلُوهُ وَهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ
وَإِذَا لَقُوا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا قَالُوا آمَنَّا
وَإِذَا خَلَا بَعْضُهُمْ إِلَىٰ بَعْضٍ قَالُوا أَتُحَدِّثُونَهُم بِمَا فَتَحَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْكُمْ
لِيُحَاجُّوكُم بِهِ عِندَ رَبِّكُمْ
أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ
أَوَلَا يَعْلَمُونَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ مَا يُسِرُّونَ وَمَا يُعْلِنُونَ
وَمِنْهُمْ أُمِّيُّونَ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ الْكِتَابَ إِلَّا أَمَانِيَّ
وَإِنْ هُمْ إِلَّا يَظُنُّونَ
فَوَيْلٌ لِّلَّذِينَ يَكْتُبُونَ الْكِتَابَ بِأَيْدِيهِمْ
ثُمَّ يَقُولُونَ هَٰذَا مِنْ عِندِ اللَّهِ
لِيَشْتَرُوا بِهِ ثَمَنًا قَلِيلًا
فَوَيْلٌ لَّهُم مِّمَّا كَتَبَتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ
وَوَيْلٌ لَّهُم مِّمَّا يَكْسِبُونَ

pages.transcription_text:
SURA AL-BAQARAH
2:80-87

(God's Chosen People?)

80 They say, “The hellfire will not touch us, save for a limited number of days.” Say, “Have you taken such a promise from God, and God never breaks His promise? Or, do you attribute to God what you know not?” 81 Yes indeed, anyone who commits sin, and becomes surrounded by his misdeeds, these shall be dwellers of the hellfire; they shall abide therein eternally. 82 As for those who believe and do good works, they shall be dwellers of Paradise; they shall abide therein eternally.

(Transgressions of the Israelites)

83 Recall that I made a covenant with the Children of Israel that they shall not worship any except God; to be kind to the parents, the relatives, the orphans, and the poor; to speak with the people amicably; to observe the Salāt and pay the Zakāt. But you turned away, except a few of you, and you became averse. 84 I made a covenant with you that you shall not shed your blood, nor shall you evict one another from your homes; you agreed and bore witness. 85 Yet, here you are slaying one another, and evicting some of you from their homes, banding together against them sinfully and defiantly. When they come to you as captives you demand ransom from them; evicting them was prohibited for you in the first place. Do you then believe in part of the scripture and disregard the other? What should be the requital for such deeds, except humiliation in this life and, on the Day of Resurrection, even worse retribution? God is never unaware of anything you do. 86 Such are they who traded away the hereafter for this lowly life. Therefore, their retribution shall not be commuted, nor shall they receive any help. 87 I have given Moses the scripture and subsequent to him I dispatched many messengers. Similarly, I gave Jesus the son of Mary manifest signs, and I supported him with the holy spirit. Is it ever so that whenever a messenger comes to you with what you do not like, you resort to arrogance? Thus, some messengers you rejected, and some you slew.

80. And they say: The Fire shall not touch us but for a few days. Say: Have you taken a promise from Allah, then Allah will not fail to keep His promise, or do you speak against Allah what you know not? 81. Yea, whoever earns evil and his sins beset him, these are the companions of the Fire; therein they shall abide. 82. And those who believe and do good deeds, these are the companions of the Garden; therein they shall abide. 83. And when We made a covenant with the Children of Israel: You shall not worship any except God; and to parents, relatives, the orphans, and the needy, show kindness; and speak to people amicably; and observe the prayer and pay the zakat. But you turned away, except a few of you, and you are averse. 84. And I made a covenant with you: You shall not shed your blood, nor shall you expel one another from your homes; you agreed and you are witnessing. 85. Then you are those who are slaying one another, and expelling a party of you from their homes, banding together against them in sin and hostility. And if they come to you as captives, you ransom them; evicting them was forbidden to you in the first place. Do you then believe in a part of the Book and disregard the other? So what is the reward of those who do such deeds, except humiliation in the life of this world, and on the Day of Resurrection, even they shall be sent to the most grievous of torment. And Allah is not unaware of anything you do. 86. These are those who buy the life of this world for the hereafter, so the torment shall not be lightened for them, nor shall they be helped. 87. And indeed We gave Moses the Book and followed him with messengers, and We gave Jesus, son of Mary, clear proofs and strengthened him with the Holy Spirit. Is it that whenever a messenger comes to you with what your souls desire not, you become arrogant? So a party you denied and a party you slay.
pages.arabic_text: وَقَالُوا لَن تَمَسَّنَا النَّارُ إِلَّا أَيَّامًا مَّعْدُودَةً ۚ قُلْ أَتَّخَذْتُمْ عِندَ اللَّهِ عَهْدًا فَلَن يُخْلِفَ اللَّهُ عَهْدَهُ ۖ أَمْ تَقُولُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ (80) بَلَىٰ مَن كَسَبَ سَيِّئَةً وَأَحَاطَتْ بِهِ خَطِيئَتُهُ فَأُولَٰئِكَ أَصْحَابُ النَّارِ ۖ هُمْ فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ (81) وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ أُولَٰئِكَ أَصْحَابُ الْجَنَّةِ ۖ هُمْ فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ (82) وَإِذْ أَخَذْنَا مِيثَاقَ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ لَا تَعْبُدُونَ إِلَّا اللَّهَ وَبِالْوَالِدَيْنِ إِحْسَانًا وَذِي الْقُرْبَىٰ وَالْيَتَامَىٰ وَالْمَسَاكِينِ وَقُولُوا لِلنَّاسِ حُسْنًا وَأَقِيمُوا الصَّلَاةَ وَآتُوا الزَّكَاةَ ثُمَّ تَوَلَّيْتُمْ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا مِّنكُمْ وَأَنتُم مُّعْرِضُونَ (83) وَإِذْ أَخَذْنَا مِيثَاقَكُمْ لَا تَسْفِكُونَ دِمَاءَكُمْ وَلَا تُخْرِجُونَ أَنفُسَكُم مِّن دِيَارِكُمْ ثُمَّ أَقْرَرْتُمْ وَأَنتُمْ تَشْهَدُونَ (84) ثُمَّ أَنتُمْ هَٰؤُلَاءِ تَقْتُلُونَ أَنفُسَكُمْ وَتُخْرِجُونَ فَرِيقًا مِّنكُم مِّن دِيَارِهِمْ تَظَاهَرُونَ عَلَيْهِم بِالْإِثْمِ وَالْعُدْوَانِ وَإِن يَأْتُوكُمْ أُسَارَىٰ تُفَادُوهُمْ وَهُوَ مُحَرَّمٌ عَلَيْكُمْ إِخْرَاجُهُمْ ۚ أَفَتُؤْمِنُونَ بِبَعْضِ الْكِتَابِ وَتَكْفُرُونَ بِبَعْضٍ ۚ فَمَا جَزَاءُ مَن يَفْعَلُ ذَٰلِكَ مِنكُمْ إِلَّا خِزْيٌ فِي الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا ۖ وَيَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ يُرَدُّونَ إِلَىٰ أَشَدِّ الْعَذَابِ ۗ وَمَا اللَّهُ بِغَافِلٍ عَمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ (85) أُولَٰئِكَ الَّذِينَ اشْتَرَوُا الْحَيَاةَ الدُّنْيَا بِالْآخِرَةِ ۖ فَلَا يُخَفَّفُ عَنْهُمُ الْعَذَابُ وَلَا هُمْ يُنصَرُونَ (86) وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنَا مُوسَى الْكِتَابَ وَقَفَّيْنَا مِن بَعْدِهِ بِالرُّسُلِ ۖ وَآتَيْنَا عِيسَى ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ الْبَيِّنَاتِ وَأَيَّدْنَاهُ بِرُوحِ الْقُدُسِ ۗ أَفَكُلَّمَا جَاءَكُمْ رَسُولٌ بِمَا لَا تَهْوَىٰ أَنفُسُكُمُ اسْتَكْبَرْتُمْ فَفَرِيقًا كَذَّبْتُمْ وَفَرِيقًا تَقْتُلُونَ (87)

pages.transcription_text:
SURA AL-BAQARAH 2:88-98

88 They said, “Our hearts are saturated.” Nay, it is but a curse from God, due to their heathenism, that causes them to believe but rarely. 89 Thus, when this scripture came to them from God, confirming what they have, and though they used to predict to the disbelievers its coming, they rejected it when they realized it had come. Such is the curse of God upon the rejectors. 90 Miserable indeed is what they traded their souls for; disbelieving in these revelations of God, out of sheer jealousy that God should bestow His grace upon whomever He wills among His creatures. Therefore, they incur wrath after wrath; the disbelievers shall suffer a humiliating punishment. 91 When they are told, “You shall believe in these revelations of God,” they say, “We believe only in what was revealed to us.” They reject subsequent scripture even though it is the truth; even though it confirms what they have. Say, “Why did you slay the prophets of God in the olden times, if you were really believers?” 92 Moses had come to you with manifest signs, but you worshiped the calf in his absence and you turned wicked. 93 Recall that I made a covenant with you, and raised Mount Sinai over you, saying, “You shall uphold this covenant strongly, and hearken.” They said, “We hearken, but we shall not obey.” Thus, their hearts were filled with adoration for the calf, due to their rebellion. Say, “Miserable is what your convictions dictate upon you, if you do have any convictions.” 94 Say, “If the abode in the hereafter is guaranteed by God for you alone, to the exclusion of all others, then you should long for death if you are truthful.” 95 However, they never long for it, due to what their hands have committed. God is fully aware of the wrong-doers. 96 In fact, you shall find them the most covetous of life, even more so than the heathens; the one of them would wish to survive a thousand years. But this shall not move him any further from his due retribution, even if he does live long. God is Seer of everything they do. 97 Say to those who resent (the archangel) Gabriel that he conveyed this Qur’an into your heart, by God’s leave, confirming previous scriptures and providing guidance and good news for the believers. 98 If anyone chooses to oppose God, His angels, and His messengers, including Gabriel and Michael, then God will oppose such disbelievers.

COMMENTARY

Predestination:

In verse 30 of sura Al-Baqarah, the Almighty announces His intention to create man. A most significant statement in this verse, though invariably overlooked by most people, is the divine declaration, "I will place on earth..." Thus, the temporary abode of man on earth had been predestined, even before his creation. God knew in advance that Adam and Eve were going to break His law by eating from the forbidden tree (verse 36). He knew that they were going to sin; thereby disqualifying themselves from abiding in heaven, and deserving to be sent down to earth (verses 36 and 38). Man, on the other hand, did not possess such advance knowledge. As far as Adam and Eve were concerned, they were placed in heaven, and given a law to live by. Therefore, in a most profound way, these verses teach us that predestination is a quality of God; Man's life, every aspect of it is indeed predestined, BUT ONLY AS FAR AS GOD IS CONCERNED. As far as we are concerned, we have the absolute freedom of thought; the absolute freedom to believe in God or disbelieve (18:29; 25:57; 39:15; 41:40; 73:19; 74:37,55; 76:29; 78:39; 80:12; 81:28). It just happens that the Almighty has foreknowledge of what course each one of us is going to choose. The dimension of "time" represents one of the limitations within which the finite man lives. But it is a nonexistent dimension with regard to the infinite God. The Almighty, therefore, exists in the past, present, and future simultaneously. Because He is in the future now, He knows the exact destiny of each one of His Creatures.

Predestination is one of the most misunderstood concepts in Islam; both by Muslims and non-Muslims. It is also one of the most abused concepts by the enemies of God; the enemies of Islam. They abuse it to project Islam as a fatalistic faith, implying the absence of freedom of choice. Consequently, such fatalistic conception of Islam is a piece of ignorance common among too many teachers and students of theology in the West.

The law given to Adam and Eve is symbolized by the forbidden tree in verse 35. Since heaven is described in the Qur'an (2:25-26; 13:35; 47:15) in allegorical terms (see also the first issue of ISLAM, page 56), the tree mentioned in verse 35 must be an allegorical representation of God's law.

The facts about man's creation as stated in verses 30 through 39 provide another example of finalization of God's message in the Qur'an. Thus, the exact reasons behind the fall of Iblis (= Lucifer = Satan) are presented to mankind for the first time. No record of such facts exists in any of the previous scriptures. As mentioned in verse 34, Iblis refused to fall prostrate before

Adam along with the other angels, due to sheer arrogance. Even such prominent Christians as evangelist Billy Graham never knew the reasons behind the fall of Lucifer. In his 1974 Arizona Crusade (aired on television June 3, 1974 in the St. Louis, Missouri area), Mr. Graham declared, "We do not know why Lucifer rebelled. It seems that he led a group of angels in rebellion against God."

That Iblis is a fallen angel is abundantly clear from verse 34, "I said to the angels, 'Fall prostrate before Adam.'" Thus, the command to fall prostrate was directed to the angels. Had Iblis been other than an angel, therefore, he would not have been expected to obey such command. The fact that Iblis was held responsible for disobedience is clear evidence that he is a fallen angel. Some students of the Qur'an maintain that Iblis is a jinn; that angels do not disobey divine commands. They base their argument on verses 12 of sura Al-A'rāf (No. 7) and 76 of sura Sād (No. 38) which state,

Iblis said, "I am better than him; You created me from fire and created him from mud."

verse 15 of sura Al-Rahmān (No. 55):

He created jinn from blazing fire

and verse 50 of sura Al-Kahf (No. 18):

I said to the angels, "Fall prostrate before Adam." They fell prostrate, except Iblis; he was a jinn; he disobeyed the command of his Lord.

However, the statement that Iblis was created from fire does not necessarily mean that he was different from the angels (who supposedly were created from light). The common belief that the angels were created from light is not supported by a single verse in the Qur'an; nowhere in the Qur'an are we told that the angels were created from light. If the source of this general belief is a Hadith or a tradition of which this commentator is unaware, this still does not necessitate that Iblis was not an angel. The Qur'an commonly refers to the various stages of man's creation [dust (3:59; 18:37; 22:5; 30:20; 35:11; 40:67), mud (6:2; 7:12; 23:12; 32:7; 37:11; 38:76; 17:61), clay (15:26; 15:28; 15:33; 55:14), drop of semen (16:4; 23:13-14; 36:77; 53:46; 75:37; 76:2; 80:19), hanging clot (96:2)]. Similarly, it is not inconceivable to describe the creation of angels at any stage (fire, light). Furthermore, from

Another lesson we derive from verses 30-39 is the grossness of the sin of PRIDE. It is because of pride, and pride alone, that an angel was doomed, and is destined for Hell. Man's refusal to surrender his will to the Creator; to fall prostrate before the Creator (not a creature), must be at least equally disastrous.

Original Sin!?

Islam holds that each individual is solely responsible for his or her deeds (6:164; 17:15; 35:18; 39:7; 53:38). This doctrine applies of course to Adam, as stated in verse 37 of sura Al-Baqarah. Adam and Eve sinned (verse 36), and they alone were held responsible. The concept of "repentance" was taught to Adam (verse 37); he exercised this concept, and his repentance was accepted by the Almighty. Thus, Adam was completely exonerated; his sin was forgiven and erased. "Original sin" (a foreign concept introduced into "Christianity"), therefore, is an unacceptable doctrine in Islam; unacceptable to the all-encompassing justice of God. Likewise, the commonly believed concept in the Judaeo-Christian world that Adam and Eve's sin of "eating the apple" refers euphemistically to sexual intercourse is unacceptable to Islam. This idea has caused millions to believe that sexual relations, even between a man and wife, are inherently sinful, and it is in part responsible for much of the sexual aberration and perversion which plagues the West.

The Origin of
Islamic Jurisprudence

What some have erroneously termed “Islamic sects” are merely branches of one tree. There is but one school of jurisprudence in Islam, that based on the life and personal conduct of the prophet Muhammad (God’s blessings and peace be upon him). It is from the extensive record of his exemplary life that the four well-known branches of Islamic jurisprudence evolved. The very initiation of these branches was approved by the Prophet himself. Thus, when he appointed Mu‘adh b. Jabal as a viceroy in Yemen, the Prophet asked him, “How will you rule?” Mu‘adh replied, “According to the Qur’an.” The Prophet said, “What if you do not find a related rule in the Qur’an?” Mu‘adh replied, “Then, I will have to depend on my personal thought and reasoning (ajtahidu).” The Prophet is reported to have been pleased and approved of Mu‘adh’s line of thinking.

In this article, the grand imām of Azhar reports on the origin and nature of the one tree of Islamic jurisprudence.

The final messenger of God (may God bestow peace and blessings upon him) practiced Islam as the Almighty wanted it to be practiced. He applied Islam to all aspects of his life; his actions, reactions, talk, feelings, and his daily conduct were all governed by Islam. The Prophet’s companions followed his example very closely. This example of the Prophet was transmitted to us from his companions to their contemporaries and then onwards from generation to generation.

The companions of the Prophet explained the Islamic way of life as they saw the Prophet live it. They narrated everything he did or said with regard to all kinds of circumstances. As the Muslim nation expanded, the Muslims transmitted these traditions to the new areas. Eventually, many outstanding scholars evolved who specialized in researching, collecting, and recording the Prophet’s traditions. Most of those scholars observed the highest

The Prophet's example was consistent with regard to certain specific situations. In other situations, however, he deliberately varied his mode of behavior. The situations where he was consistent include all the fard (the obligatory rites of worship). These encompass such rites as the method of fasting, the recitation of Qur'an during the ṣalāt, and the kneeling for "tashuhhud" recitation.

The variability in the Prophet's example was observed only with regard to the nonobligatory functions which are designated today as "sunnah." Thus, his conduct did not follow one specific methodology in such sunnahs as reciting supplications between the initial takbīr of ṣalāt (saying, "Allāh Akbar") and the opening sura (Al-Fātiḥah), and in his supplications as he fell prostrate in ṣalāt, and in the manner of placing the arms and hands during ṣalāt, and so forth. Such variations were observed also in many situations of daily life involving commerce, crimes, loans, usury, and personal relations. it is only around these variations in sunnah that the four branches of jurisprudence evolved. No differences whatsoever exist among the opinions of the imams Al-Shāfi'ī, Mālik, Abū Ḥanifah, and ibn Ḥanbal concerning the obligatory duties. Their differences are found only in their personal interpretation and reasoning with regard to the nonobligatory actions and behavior of the Prophet.

These non-doctrinal differences of opinion among the four great imams have been grossly exaggerated by various groups who sought to create imaginary sects or divisions within Islam. Such exaggerations were intended mainly to divert the Muslims from their basic Islamic doctrines and, hence, from establishing the perfect society as inculcated by Islam. It was such groups who created, for example, the question of whether one should fold or unfold the arms while standing in ṣalāt. In the folding situation, the worshiper places the left hand on the stomach and the right hand on the back of the left hand. In the unfolding situation, the worshiper simply lets the arms hang down freely on the sides. This minor issue was magnified by some researchers beyond reasonable proportions, and led to lengthy and hot debates in certain Muslim countries. These arguments were finally terminated when one enlightened scholar raised the following questions to those involved in the controversy:
1. If the worshiper stood in ṣalāt with his arms extended straight forward, would that nullify the prayer?
2. If the arms were lifted completely upward, would that nullify the prayer?

THE ORIGIN OF ISLAMIC JURISPRUDENCE

3. If the arms were folded, would the prayer be nullified?
4. If the arms hang down on the sides, would that nullify the prayer?
When the debaters unanimously agreed that the answer to each of these questions was “No”, they realized the insignificance of their differences.
This question of placing one’s arms during the ṣalāt prayer is a typical example of the subjects in which the great imams of jurisprudence expressed varied opinions. It is such differences of opinion, originating from the traditions of the Prophet, that became the basis of the branches in Islamic jurisprudence.
Clearly, all these branches, reflecting different personal interpretations, belong to one and the same tree. All the imams of jurisprudence had but a single model from which they derived their opinions. Only ignorance and narrow-mindedness would create separate schools of jurisprudence out of the one school, namely, the school of prophet Muḥammad (God’s peace and blessings be upon him). It is heartening to note that the era of false divisions within the school of Islamic jurisprudence has passed. It is a rarity nowadays to meet a Muslim who describes himself as a Shāfi‘i, Mālikī, Ḥanafī, or Ḥanbalī; the trend has been towards the one essential description: Muslim.

Who Qualifies as a Mujtahid?
By a mujtahid here is meant one who is scholarly qualified to set new rules and regulations to be followed by the Muslims everywhere. Some scholars have contended that the door of ijtihād (personal thought and reasoning which leads to new rules) has been closed; that the last mujtahids were the four well-known imams. Other scholars maintain that the door of ijtihād is always open. Some among the latter group, however, talk about ijtihād as if it were attainable by anyone. It is inconceivable that God’s grace was limited to the four great imams with regard to ijtihād, since new circumstances are founded with each generation of humans. Therefore, any Muslim who satisfies certain exacting requirements can contribute to the rules and regulations known as Islamic jurisprudence, i.e., become a mujtahid. These requirements include:
1. Mastery of the Arabic language: The great imams of jurisprudence (e.g. Mālik and Al-Shāfi‘i) were unrivaled masters of the Arabic linguistic sciences.
2. Memorization of the Qur’an, with full awareness of the complete message and regulations therein. This includes a high degree of knowledge of the various Qur’anic sciences such as the circumstances associated with the revelation of each verse or group of verses. Although the Qur’an was revealed for the guidance of all the people in all places and at all times, knowledge of the specific circumstances of revelation does help in reaching

the correct interpretation.
3. Knowledge of the spoken sunnah, as well as the practical traditions of the Prophet (God’s peace and blessings be upon him).
These requirements form the basic background needed by a Muslim before he or she can contribute correctly to Islamic jurisprudence.

The seriousness and the awesomeness of responsibility in issuing new rules of jurisprudence can be appreciated if we reflect upon some of the Prophet’s teachings in this regard. In Ṣaḥīḥ Al-Shaykhān (well-known record of Ḥadīth), the Prophet (may God bestow peace and blessings upon him) is reported as saying, “Whoever fabricates false rules from my teachings shall be committing a gross offense.” Abū Hurayrah reported the Prophet’s saying, “Whoever establishes a righteous tradition shall receive a reward equal to that due to all followers of such tradition, without reduction in their rewards. And whoever establishes an evil tradition shall incur sins equal to all the sins of those who follow such evil tradition, without reducing their guilt (reported in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim).

The overall purpose of ijtihād can be divided into 2 areas:
1. Establishing rules of Islamic jurisprudence relating to matters which took place during the Prophet’s time. In this case, the purpose would be to find the Prophet’s judgment regarding the matter in question. An example here would be the search for the exact manner of making ablution (wuḍū’), as performed by the Prophet (may God bestow peace and blessings upon him).
2. Establishing rules of Islamic jurisprudence dealing with current matters which did not exist during the Prophet’s time. Even here, the rule-making process must depend on the Prophet’s example through Qiyās (analogy). The Qur’an and the sunnah of the holy Prophet provide an unlimited array of situations which can be used directly or indirectly in establishing current rules of Islamic jurisprudence. Thus, the Muslim never lacks the reference materials he needs to establish a given rule. Under all circumstances, the mujtahid must be a “follower,” rather than an “initiator.” For the Prophet’s instructions to the mujtahids are, “you shall follow, not invent” when dealing with rules of Islamic jurisprudence.

Finally, it must be pointed out that ijtihād cannot succeed through knowledge alone. A mujtahid must be characterized first and foremost by a high standard of piety and righteousness. All the great imams who contributed positively to Islamic jurisprudence had in common a high level of genuine piety. Thus, the rules they have established for us represent no less than guidance from God to His sincere servants. Knowledge alone can never invoke such divine guidance, for God tells us, “only those who stand by God shall receive right guidance.” (Qur’an [3:101]).

The Aphorisms
of Salāmah Al-Rāḍī : 2

These aphorisms, with their esoteric connotations, are derived from the Qur'an, the sunna, teachings of the great imams, and the principles of Sufism. Published for the first time in English, these particular aphorisms are valuable pieces of advice delivered by one of the greatest Sufis of all time, Shaykh Salāmah Al-Rāḍī, to his dervishes.

11. My beloved in (the cause of) God: If anyone of you wishes God to heed his prayers, he shall first heed God's commands. When you heed Him, He heeds you.

12. My beloved ones: Whoever claims to have acquired dignity on his own, reveals but sinful pride. But whoever humbles himself before His Master, derives his dignity from his Lord. When The Reality sees you humbling yourself before Him, He permits no humiliation to ever touch you; He guarantees your dignity.

13. My beloved in (the cause of) God: Once your hearts are fully content with your Master, you enter the court of His grace. For as long as you are hesitant, you remain strangers to Him. He is only with those who are fully with him.

14. O you beloved ones: If your heart truly loves your Master, it will not grieve over parting with anything else. So long as you grieve over parting with other than your Master, this should be your indicator that you are not yet in His court. Rather, you would be in the court of whatever diverted you from your Master.

15. O you beloved ones: If you are saddened by the people's criticism, and rejoice when they flatter you, beware. This would indicate that your ego is still alive and thus still competing with the Master in His divine attributes.

16. O you beloved ones: If you spend your lives worshiping your Master, while at the same time being dissatisfied with Him, not humbling yourselves before His dignity, staying away from His company, keeping your thoughts with the devils and the far-removed individuals, how do you expect your worship to attain any light? It would be spiritless worship; dead.

17. O you beloved ones: You care too much for feeding vanishing shells, and pay little attention to feeding your eternal entity. Consequently, you end up with great bodies, but diminished souls.

18. O you beloved ones: Your hearts are like empty containers. You strive and even pay monies to fill them with darkness, while the light is within your reach, free of charge. Instead of helping yourselves to the light, you keep pushing your hearts further and further therefrom. Would a wise person fill his eyes with darkness, until he sees but darkness? Or, would he rather fill them with light in order to become a seer?

19. O beloved ones: The love of this life has a certain sweetness which causes intoxication of the heart. Thus, it becomes distracted from the love of its Master, and adores but illusions. This world is no more than an illusion. Therefore, you shall not imbibe this particular wine; it is far more evil than the grape's wine which masks the mind from physical objects.

20. My beloved in (the path to) God: Whenever you see one who obeys the devil & does his deeds, you shall stay clear of him; he is a devil himself. Whoever befriends him shall in turn become a devil like him.

21. O you beloved ones: Whoever is filled with goodness, nothing but goodness comes out of him. Whoever is filled with evil, nothing but evil comes out of him. How could evil ever spill out of one who is filled with goodness?

22. O you beloved ones: Whoever adorns himself with virtue exhibits but virtue. Therefore, you shall strive to become virtuous people, so that only virtuous traits may be reflected from you.

23. My beloved ones: The poor, by definition, is one who is in need. Thus, if one possesses tremendous wealth but still seeks more wealth, he is poor. He continues to labor in order to acquire more riches. If he is never satisfied, his poverty will last all his life.

24. O you beloved ones: Whoever seeks power tires himself, for power is beloved by all, and the people fight among themselves over it. Therefore, you should not seek power. It will seek you so long as you shun seeking it, and when anyone opposes you in this case, many will stand by you and support you.

25. My beloved ones: If anyone claims superiority over you, do not fight him. If you fight him over it, it will abandon both you and him. But if you allow him to claim superiority, it will abandon him and come to you.

26. My beloved ones: If anyone fights you over what belongs to God, you shall not fight him. God cares for whatever belongs to Him, & if you take the matter in your hands and fight over His belongings, you yourselves belong to God no more.

27. My beloved ones: You gain God's love if you are persecuted in His cause. Thus, you shall seek victory for His cause. You shall never seek victory for yourselves. If you do, you fall from your Master's grace.

28. My beloved ones: You shall persevere in the face of persecution, injustice, and tribulation. Do not ever execrate or curse. Instead, you shall be exemplars of mercy and pardon on earth, in order to earn the love of your Master. The Almighty is always with those whose hearts are broken in His cause.

29. My beloved ones: While the people are busy with the affairs of this life, you shall busy yourselves with your Master. While they are busy with the given, you shall be busy with the Giver.

30. My beloved ones: Habituate yourselves with doing good, & respond not to evil by evil. God loves the good-doers.

The Invocations of ‘Abdullāh Anṣārī : 2

‘Abdullāh Anṣārī, a famous Persian Sufi, was born in Herat 396 AH (1005 C.E.). It is said that one of his ancestors was a companion of the prophet Muhammad (God’s blessings and peace be upon him) who moved to Herat with ‘Aṣaf, son of Qays. Anṣārī’s father, Abu Manṣūr Muhammad Anṣārī, became a permanent resident of Herat.

These invocations, translated into English by Sir Jogendra Singh, contain true advice to guide the Pilgrim along the path of discipleship to the temple of peace. They come from a man who himself had trodden the path and found what his heart desired.

When ‘Abdullāh Anṣārī departed from this world, he was 85 years old, leaving behind a wealth of Sufi knowledge. Among his well-known works are Risāla Munājāt (The Book of Prayer), Tabaqat-ul-Ṣūfiyyah (The Book of Sufis), Zād-ul-‘Ārifīn (Provisions of the Sufi Teachers), and Kitāb-i-Isrār (The Book of Mysteries).

O Lord, give me a heart
That I may pour it out in thanksgiving.
Give me life
That I may spend it
in working for the salvation of the world.
O Lord, give me that right discrimination
That the Lure of the world may cheat me no more.
Give me strength
That my faith suffer no eclipse.
O Lord, give me understanding,
That I stray not from the path.
Give me light
To avoid pitfalls.
O Lord, keep watch over me
That I stray not.
Keep me on the path of righteousness
That I escape from the pangs of repentance.
